title: VRVLOG_avatar_animator 1
description: The avatar's VRChat FX controller, Expression Menu and Expression Parameters as written in the avatar, read by the exporter from the prepared copy. Every index points into a table of this extension: parameters, menus, the layer's machines and states, motions, clips and targets; -1 means none where allowed. Machines of a layer are flattened in preorder: machine 0 is the layer's root with parent -1 and no exit transitions, every other machine follows its parent. Entry and exit transitions carry no timing; state and Any State transitions do. Every transition has exactly one of toState, toMachine and exit. Only transitions Unity can take are written, in Unity's order: Mute and Solo are already applied, and a transition without a destination or with a condition Unity cannot read is left out. A condition's mode fits its parameter's type: if on a bool or trigger, ifNot on a bool, greater and less on a float or int, equals and notEqual on an int. A state's speed, cycle offset and time parameters are floats and its mirror parameter is a bool. The parameter table holds the Expression Parameters and the FX controller's parameters only; a blend tree, direct weight or state option on a name the FX controller does not declare is written as Unity plays it (a blend tree with no motion, a direct child left out, a state option left unset), except that Unity plays such a tree held by another tree by what the other children leave. That case, and a parameter of another type, where Unity reads an unrelated float, are written the same way and counted as unreadParameter. A Parameter Driver operation on an undeclared name, or a copy without a source, is counted as operation. Clips keep curves for GameObject activeSelf, for float FX parameters and for the BlendShape weights the FX moves on a mesh of the file, for the enabled flag of a mesh renderer and for a float, a color channel or a texture scale and offset channel of a material property of a mesh renderer, one curve per track and target, with at most 16384 keys and 4096 tracks per clip, given to activeSelf curves first, then to parameter curves, then to BlendShape curves, then to renderer enabled curves, then to material float curves (one material curve takes one track of the room however many targets it moves), then to the enabled curves of constraints in VRVLOG_avatar_constraints, then to material color and texture channel curves; a curve that does not fit is counted (other for activeSelf, parameter for a float parameter, blendShape for a BlendShape, enabled for a renderer's or a constraint's enabled flag, material for a material curve); other curves and unsupported behaviours are counted in omitted by kind, in the order of the enumeration, and leave out kinds with no entries. An active, morph, enabled or material target's rest is the value (activeSelf, the BlendShape weight, the renderer's enabled flag or the material's value) before the exporter changed the avatar. A material curve moves a property the full lilToon contract (LilToonFullContract) keeps for the app's material under the same name and type: a float (material.X), a color channel (material.X.r) or a channel of a texture's scale and offset (material.X_ST.x); a curve on another name, or with another type, is counted as materialProperty, and one on a feature switch the app fixes when it loads the material (LilToonFullContract.Switches) as materialSwitch. A material curve is counted as material when none of its renderer's materials the file writes has the property, when a clip of an additive layer moves one of its targets, or when another curve of the same clip already moved each of its targets; a vector channel curve is counted as material too. A BlendShape is counted as blendShape instead when the base geometry already shows its end weight and no reverse morph target takes it back to 0, when shapes that disagree on rest, baked or end were merged into one, when it has several frames, when it is a lip sync shape, which the base geometry also takes the other lip sync shapes and the default mouth off, when a clip of an additive layer moves it, as its reference pose is not carried, or when another mesh has a shape of the same name the FX does not move and the shape is on another renderer after optimization, as a merge may have put both into one output; a curve on a mesh with no node in the file is counted as missingNode; a BlendShape of several frames is counted too, as it need not be linear between baked and end, and a curve that holds rest is written like any other, but a target whose curves all hold rest on a base that shows it (baked equal to rest) is written only when its morph target is in the file for another reason. A BlendShape has its weight here only: when a VRM expression binds the same morph target, how the two combine is the reader's choice. Every FX parameter that a clip of the controller animates is a parameter target, with or without tracks; an Avatar Mask is not written, as Unity applies it to none of these targets. expressions lists custom expressions of VRMC_vrm by name, each with the clips it was read from and the ways into the FX states that play one of them, directly or in a blend tree: the layer's first state (default), an entry transition of a machine (entry), an Any State transition (any) or a state's transition (state), with that transition's conditions; a transition to a machine is not followed, and the same way with the same conditions is listed once. A state listed there plays one of the expression's clips, and a condition there takes the types a transition's condition takes. Rules that span entries are validated by the shared reader (AvatarAnimatorData.Read): index ranges, blend trees without cycles and nested at most 32 deep (a tree of clips is 1 deep), unique targets per clip, unique (node, property) over active targets, unique (node, morph) over morph targets and unique parameter over parameter targets, unique (node, component) over renderer enabled targets and (component, index) over constraint enabled targets, unique (material, name) over materialFloat targets, unique (material, name, channel) over materialColor and over materialTextureST targets, end different from baked, a parameter target's rest and tracks fitting its type, Prevent Repeats only on a random into an int, and a layer's syncedLayer naming another layer of the same controller that is not synced itself, a motion that expands to at most 4096 motions when its blend trees are expanded per parent, and the parameter types above. Node indices of active, morph and enabled targets must be less than the glTF node count, a material target's material must be less than the glTF material count, and a morph target's node must have a mesh with more than morph targets.

controllers.description: The FX first, then the Gesture and the Action the avatar has a custom controller for, each at most once and in that order. The expressions name layers of the FX.

menu.description: The menu a subMenu control opens; only subMenu controls have it, and it may be absent.

omitted.description: A Gesture or Action controller only, and only when not empty: what the exporter left out while reading this controller that changes which transitions it takes: the kinds parameter, operation and unreadParameter in that order, then a kind a newer exporter adds, each once. Other kinds of the controller, the FX's omissions and those of the extension as a whole stay in the root omitted. A reader that plays the controllers tells from this whose transitions an omission changes.

layer.description: A synced layer (syncedLayer >= 0) holds a copy of its source layer's machines, with its own motions and state behaviours. A layer is never synced to itself, and the source is the layer that owns the machines: where Unity syncs a layer to another synced layer, syncedLayer names the layer at the end of that chain.

weight.description: The default weight. The first layer is always 1, as Unity plays it whatever its default weight says.

blending.description: The first layer is always override, as Unity does not take its blending mode into account.

syncedLayer.description: The index of the source layer in the same controller, or -1 when the layer is not synced.

syncedLayerAffectsTiming.description: Unity's Timing option of a synced layer; false when the layer is not synced.

mask.description: The layer's AvatarMask; a layer without one moves everything, as does a mask that lets every body part move and names no transforms. humanoid lists the body parts it lets move (Unity's AvatarMaskBodyPart: 0 Root, 1 Body, 2 Head, 3 LeftLeg, 4 RightLeg, 5 LeftArm, 6 RightArm, 7 LeftFingers, 8 RightFingers, 9 LeftFootIK, 10 RightFootIK, 11 LeftHandIK, 12 RightHandIK), nodes the nodes its transform mask lets move; a transform the file has no node for is left out. Without nodes the mask names no transforms and lets every node move. Each list is in increasing order.

anyStateTransitions.description: The Any State transitions of the layer, held by the root machine (machine 0) alone: Unity never takes one that a machine inside another holds. They apply to the whole layer whatever state it is in, and are looked at before the transitions of the current state.

oneOf.description: One key per tracking part, from the SDK field name without the tracking prefix (trackingHead is head). A part is never named type.

preventRepeats.description: Prevent Repeats (VRChat SDK 3.10.2 and later): a random never sets the value it set last. True only on a random into an int, the one place the SDK offers it; false everywhere else and for an SDK without the setting. Data written before the setting was read has none, which is read as false.

source.description: The parameter a copy reads. A copy has one and no other type has.

parameters.description: One for 1d, two for the 2d types, none for direct. Each is a float parameter.

children.description: Children of a direct tree have directParameter, a float parameter; others do not.

cycleOffset.description: The clip's Cycle Offset (Animation Clip settings), as a fraction of its length.

key.description: [time, value, inTangent, outTangent, inWeight, outWeight]. A null tangent is stepped.

target.description: active: the node's activeSelf, rest 0 or 1. parameter: FX parameter `parameter`, which a clip of the controller animates; it has no node. rest is the controller's default for it, a value of its type (0 or 1 for a bool or trigger), and may differ from the parameter's default when Expression Parameters also declare it. Unity moves only a float parameter by a curve, so only a float target has tracks; a curve on an int, bool or trigger holds it at rest. While any clip animates a parameter, the animator owns it: menus, Parameter Drivers and the app do not change it, and it is rest whenever no layer writes it. morph: morph target `morph` of the mesh on `node`, as in morphTargetBinds. a morph target's rest is the Unity BlendShape weight when no layer writes it; the base geometry already holds the weight `baked`, and the glTF weight 1 shows the weight `end`, so an animated weight v is the glTF weight (v - baked) / (end - baked), not clamped. When the base holds a shape at its end weight, the morph target is the reverse one the export adds, which takes the base back to weight 0, and end is 0. enabled: the enabled flag of `component` on `node`, rest 0 or 1; component renderer is the renderer the node draws, and it shows only while the node and its parents are also active (enabled is not inherited). materialFloat: the float shader property `name` of glTF material `material`, rest its value in the exported material; it has no node. Unity animates a renderer's material property for every material of that renderer, so a curve becomes a track of each target of a material the renderer draws with that has the property; materials shared by renderers share the target. materialColor: channel `channel` (r, g, b or a) of the color shader property `name` of glTF material `material`. materialTextureST: channel `channel` of the scale and offset of the texture shader property `name` (Unity's name_ST: x and y the scale, z and w the offset). Each is one float like materialFloat, with rest its value in the exported material. materialSlot: material slot `slot` (a submesh, in order) of the mesh on `node`; rest and every key are the index of the glTF material the slot draws with, -1 for none. It is never interpolated: in a blend tree it takes the value of the motion of the greatest weight, and over a transition, a layer or the FX weight the next value once its weight passes 0.5. A slot swapped to a material of a shader other than official lilToon is counted as materialSlotShader, and one swapped to a material the file does not write as material. translation, rotation, scale: channel `channel` of the local position, rotation or scale of `node`, in Unity's space as the animation curve holds it (not glTF's), rest its value when the file is written; each is one float. translation and scale name x, y or z. A rotation without euler is a quaternion channel (x, y, z or w) that a reader blends as written and normalizes; with euler true it is an angle in degrees (x, y or z, Unity's localEulerAnglesRaw) that a reader blends as an angle and turns into a rotation with Quaternion.Euler, and rest is the angles the Unity inspector shows. The rotation targets of one node are all Euler or all quaternion: when the controller moves a node both ways its rotation curves are counted as rotationMixed. A curve on a Humanoid bone is counted as humanoidTransform, and one on the avatar root or of another rotation interpolation as transform. An enabled target with component constraint is the enabled flag of entry `index` of VRVLOG_avatar_constraints, whose node it names; a curve on a constraint that table does not have is counted as enabled. muscle: Humanoid muscle `muscle`, an index of Unity's HumanTrait.MuscleName (0 to 94), which a clip of a layer that is not additive moves; it has no node, and rest is the T-pose's 0. A clip names a finger muscle as LeftHand.Thumb.1 Stretched where HumanTrait.MuscleName says Left Thumb 1 Stretched. Any other property, or enabled of another component (an enabled target always names its component as a string) is a kind a newer exporter may write: a reader takes it without looking at its other keys, reads rest when it is a number, lets clips move it and writes it nowhere, and keeps its keys when it writes the file again.

kind.description: One of blendShape, material, transform, enabled, parameter, muscle, other, missingNode, behaviour, operation, unreadParameter, materialProperty, materialSwitch, materialSlotShader, humanoidTransform, rotationMixed and humanoidRoot, in that order. muscle counts the Animator curves on the avatar root that are no Humanoid muscle the file writes (a curve past a clip's room, one on an additive layer, a translation DoF or a name no controller declares); humanoidRoot those of the root's position and rotation (RootT, RootQ, MotionT, MotionQ) and of the hands' and feet's IK goals, which the app's tracking places. A kind a newer exporter adds comes after them, each once; a reader keeps it.

name.description: A key of VRMC_vrm expressions.custom; unique.

clips.description: Indices into clips, in increasing order.
